publications.name: Possible photometric signatures of nebular-dominated emission in 1.5 < z < 8.5 JADES galaxies
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Developed a new photometric method to search for high-redshift galaxies whose light is dominated by nebular continuum emission, a possible signature of a top-heavy initial mass function in the early Universe.

publications.name: Reionization in protocluster environments at z > 7 with JWST/NIRSpec
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Identified two galaxy protoclusters at z > 7 in the JADES Deep Survey and showed their member galaxies produce ionizing photons more efficiently than typical field galaxies, suggesting protoclusters may have driven local reionization.

publications.name: Galaxy mergers in the epoch of reionization – II. Merger-triggered star formation and AGN activities at z = 4.5−8.5
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Used a sample of over 3,000 galaxies across eight JWST fields to show that galaxy mergers boost both star formation and active galactic nucleus activity in the early Universe at z = 4.5-8.5.

publications.name: EPOCHS. III. Unbiased UV Continuum Slopes at 6.5 < z < 13 from Combined PEARLS GTO and Public JWST/NIRCam Imaging
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Measured UV continuum slopes for over 1,000 galaxies at 6.5 < z < 13 from the EPOCHS survey, correcting for a photometric bias that can make faint high-redshift galaxies appear artificially blue.

publications.name: Cosmic stillness: high quiescent galaxy fractions across upper mass scales in the early Universe to z = 7 with JWST
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Identified 90 candidate quiescent (quenched) galaxies at 3 < z < 7 using JWST data, finding surprisingly high fractions of massive galaxies had already shut down star formation in the early Universe.

publications.name: New methods of identifying AGN in the early Universe using spectroscopy and photometry in the JWST era
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Explored new spectroscopic and photometric methods for identifying active galactic nuclei in the early Universe, showing that standard optical diagnostics break down in JWST's low-metallicity, high-redshift regime.

publications.name: JWSTs PEARLS: NIRCam imaging and NIRISS spectroscopy of a z = 3.6 star-forming galaxy lensed into a near-Einstein ring by a z = 1.258 massive elliptical galaxy
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Reported the discovery of a rare near-Einstein ring gravitational lens in JWST-PEARLS data, in which a z = 1.258 elliptical galaxy lenses a background z = 3.6 star-forming galaxy into four images.

publications.name: Behind the spotlight: a systematic assessment of outshining using NIRCam medium bands in the JADES Origins Field
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Used deep medium-band JWST imaging of the JADES Origins Field to systematically test how much bright young stars can ‘outshine’ and bias stellar mass estimates for more than 200 high-redshift galaxies.

publications.name: The impact of medium-width bands on the selection and subsequent luminosity function measurements of high-z galaxies
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Showed that adding medium-width JWST/NIRCam photometric bands substantially improves the reliability of high-redshift galaxy selection and the resulting luminosity function measurements.

publications.name: Lonely Little Red Dots: Challenges to the Active Galactic Nucleus Nature of Little Red Dots through Their Clustering and Spectral Energy Distributions
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal Letters
publications.summary: Studied the clustering and spectral properties of 124 ‘little red dots’ seen with JWST and found they cluster like normal star-forming galaxies rather than luminous quasars, challenging the idea that they are predominantly powered by active galactic nuclei.

publications.name: Galaxy mergers in the epoch of reionization – I. A JWST study of pair fractions, merger rates, and stellar mass accretion rates at z = 4.5–11.5
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Measured galaxy merger pair fractions and rates across eight JWST fields at z = 4.5-11.5, extending merger statistics to the earliest cosmic epochs yet studied.

publications.name: EPOCHS. XI. The Structure and Morphology of Galaxies in the Epoch of Reionization to z ∼ 12.5
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Measured the sizes and structural (Sérsic) properties of 520 galaxies at 6.5 < z < 12.5 from the EPOCHS survey, tracing how galaxy morphology evolves during the epoch of reionization.

publications.name: EPOCHS. I. The Discovery and Star-forming Properties of Galaxies in the Epoch of Reionization at 6.5 < z < 18 with PEARLS and Public JWST Data
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Presented the discovery, properties, and public catalog of 1,165 galaxies at 6.5 < z < 18 identified in deep JWST NIRCam imaging combining the PEARLS survey with public JWST fields.

publications.name: Like a candle in the wind: the embers of once aflame, now smouldering galaxies at 5 < z < 8
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Introduced a photometric method to find faint, temporarily quiescent ‘smouldering’ dwarf galaxies at 5 < z < 8 in deep JADES imaging, galaxies whose star formation has recently and briefly switched off.

publications.name: EPOCHS. IV. SED Modeling Assumptions and Their Impact on the Stellar Mass Function at 6.5 ≤ z ≤ 13.5 Using PEARLS and Public JWST Observations
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Used a sample of 1,120 galaxy candidates at 6.5 < z < 13.5 to place some of the first direct constraints on the galaxy stellar mass function beyond z = 10, and examined how different SED-fitting assumptions change the result.

publications.name: EPOCHS Paper V. The dependence of galaxy formation on galaxy structure at z < 7 from JWST observations
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Examined how a galaxy's structure and morphology relate to its star formation history at z < 7, using a morphologically classified catalog of nearly 4,000 JWST/CEERS galaxies.

publications.name: EPOCHS Paper – VIII. An insight into MIRI-selected galaxies in SMACS-0723 and the benefits of deep MIRI photometry in revealing AGN and the dusty universe
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Analyzed 181 galaxies selected with JWST's Mid-Infrared Instrument in the SMACS-0723 field, showing that deep MIRI photometry helps reveal dust emission and AGN activity missed by near-infrared data alone.

publications.name: EPOCHS. II. The Ultraviolet Luminosity Function from 7.5 < z < 13.5 Using 180 arcmin2 of Deep, Blank Fields from the PEARLS Survey and Public JWST Data
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Measured the ultraviolet luminosity function and cosmic star formation rate density of galaxies at 7.5 < z < 13.5 using a large combined dataset from the PEARLS survey and public JWST fields.

publications.name: Adding value to JWST spectra and photometry: stellar population and star formation properties of spectroscopically confirmed JADES and CEERS galaxies at z > 7
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Combined JWST spectroscopy and photometry for 43 confirmed galaxies at z > 7 to test how well photometrically derived stellar population and star-formation properties match spectroscopic measurements.

publications.name: A Robust Study of High-redshift Galaxies: Unsupervised Machine Learning for Characterizing Morphology with JWST up to z ∼ 8
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Applied unsupervised machine learning to characterize the morphologies of high-redshift JWST galaxies out to z ~ 8, offering a data-driven alternative to traditional visual classification schemes.

publications.name: Galaxy Quenching at the High Redshift Frontier: A Fundamental Test of Cosmological Models in the Early Universe with JWST-CEERS
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal
publications.summary: Used advanced statistical methods, including random forest classification, on JWST-CEERS data to test what drives the quenching of massive galaxies within the first few billion years of cosmic history.

publications.name: EPOCHS IX. When cosmic dawn breaks: evidence for evolved stellar populations in 7 < z < 12 galaxies from PEARLS GTO and public NIRCam imaging
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Searched PEARLS and public JWST/NIRCam imaging for galaxies at 7 < z < 12 showing a Balmer break, a signature of an already-evolved stellar population surprisingly early in cosmic history.

publications.name: On the observability and identification of Population III galaxies with JWST
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Used theoretical models of Population III stars to predict how JWST imaging and spectroscopy could identify these hypothesized first-generation, metal-free galaxies.

publications.name: A Large Population of Faint 8 < z < 16 Galaxies Found in the First JWST NIRCam Observations of the NGDEEP Survey
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal Letters
publications.summary: Presented the discovery of 16 new galaxy candidates at z > 8.5, including one of the most distant galaxies then known at z ~ 15.6, in the first deep JWST NIRCam imaging of the NGDEEP survey.

publications.name: Seeing sharper and deeper: JWST’s first glimpse of the photometric and spectroscopic properties of galaxies in the epoch of reionization
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Analyzed the photometric and spectroscopic properties of four spectroscopically confirmed galaxies in the epoch of reionization, showing that F115W imaging is key to distinguishing genuine high-redshift galaxies from lower-redshift contaminants.

publications.name: Discovery and properties of ultra-high redshift galaxies (9 < z < 12) in the JWST ERO SMACS 0723 Field
publications.publisher: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
publications.summary: Searched the JWST Early Release Observations of the SMACS 0723 field and discovered four candidate galaxies at z > 9, among the first ultra-high-redshift galaxies found with JWST.

publications.name: Panic! at the Disks: First Rest-frame Optical Observations of Galaxy Structure at z > 3 with JWST in the SMACS 0723 Field
publications.publisher: The Astrophysical Journal Letters
publications.summary: Presented the first rest-frame optical morphological study of galaxies at z > 3 using JWST's Early Release Observations of the SMACS 0723 field.
